+from __future__ import (absolute_import, division, print_function)
+__metaclass__ = type
+
+import pytest
+
+from ansible.module_utils.facts.hardware import freebsd, netbsd, openbsd
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('hardware_module,hardware_class,fact_methods', [
+    (freebsd, freebsd.FreeBSDHardware,
+     ('get_cpu_facts', 'get_memory_facts', 'get_dmi_facts',
+      'get_device_facts', 'get_mount_facts')),
+    (netbsd, netbsd.NetBSDHardware,
+     ('get_cpu_facts', 'get_memory_facts', 'get_dmi_facts', 'get_mount_facts')),
+    (openbsd, openbsd.OpenBSDHardware,
+     ('get_processor_facts', 'get_memory_facts', 'get_dmi_facts',
+      'get_device_facts', 'get_mount_facts')),
+])
+def test_bsd_populate_includes_uptime_and_other_facts(mocker, hardware_module,
+                                                      hardware_class, fact_methods):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    if hardware_module is openbsd:
+        mocker.patch.object(hardware_module, 'get_sysctl', return_value={})
+        mocker.patch.object(hardware_class, 'get_uptime_facts',
+                            return_value={'uptime_seconds': 125})
+    else:
+        mocker.patch.object(hardware_module, 'get_uptime_facts',
+                            return_value={'uptime_seconds': 125})
+    if hardware_module is netbsd:
+        mocker.patch.object(hardware_module, 'get_sysctl', return_value={})
+    for index, method in enumerate(fact_methods):
+        mocker.patch.object(hardware_class, method, return_value={'source_%s' % index: True})
+
+    facts = hardware_class(module).populate()
+
+    assert facts['uptime_seconds'] == 125
+    for index in range(len(fact_methods)):
+        assert facts['source_%s' % index] is True

@@ -0,0 +1,71 @@
+from __future__ import (absolute_import, division, print_function)
+__metaclass__ = type
+
+import errno
+
+import pytest
+
+from ansible.module_utils.facts.sysctl import get_sysctl, get_uptime_facts
+
+
+def test_get_sysctl_formats_and_continuations(mocker):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    module.run_command.return_value = (0, 'hw.ncpu=4\nkern.osrelease: 7.5\n'
+                                        'vm.swappiness = 60\nhw.model Example CPU\n'
+                                        '  second line\nbadline\nhw.usermem=1024\n', '')
+
+    assert get_sysctl(module, ['hw', 'kern']) == {
+        'hw.ncpu': '4', 'kern.osrelease': '7.5',
+        'vm.swappiness': '60', 'hw.model': 'Example CPU\n  second line',
+        'hw.usermem': '1024',
+    }
+    module.warn.assert_called_once_with(
+        'Unable to split sysctl line (badline): not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1)')
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('failure,warning', [
+    ((1, '', 'permission denied'), 'Unable to read sysctl: permission denied'),
+    (OSError('unavailable'), 'Unable to read sysctl: unavailable'),
+    (IOError('unavailable'), 'Unable to read sysctl: unavailable'),
+])
+def test_get_sysctl_command_failure(mocker, failure, warning):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    if isinstance(failure, tuple):
+        module.run_command.return_value = failure
+    else:
+        module.run_command.side_effect = failure
+    assert get_sysctl(module, ['hw']) == {}
+    module.warn.assert_called_once_with(warning)
+
+
+def test_get_uptime_facts(mocker):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    module.run_command.return_value = (0, '100\n', '')
+    mocker.patch('ansible.module_utils.facts.sysctl.time.time', return_value=225)
+
+    assert get_uptime_facts(module) == {'uptime_seconds': 125}
+    module.run_command.assert_called_once_with(['/sbin/sysctl', '-n', 'kern.boottime'])
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('result', [(1, '100', 'failed'), (0, '', ''),
+                                    (0, '{ sec = 100 }', ''), (0, 'abc', '')])
+def test_get_uptime_facts_omits_invalid_output(mocker, result):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    module.run_command.return_value = result
+    assert get_uptime_facts(module) == {}
+
+
+def test_get_uptime_facts_missing_binary(mocker):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = None
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        get_uptime_facts(module)
+
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/missing/sysctl'
+    module.run_command.side_effect = OSError(errno.ENOENT, 'No such file')
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        get_uptime_facts(module)
